job.title: Class 5 Driver
job.description:
Good Hours. Variety. Solid Team. Steady Work.

Are you a Class 5 driver looking for a role where no two weeks are quite the same?

We're recruiting on behalf of a well-established, proudly Kiwi-owned transport business with a reputation for doing things right and looking after its people. If you're after job security, variety in your work, and a supportive team environment, this could be the opportunity you've been looking for.

What's in it for you?

✔ Consistent 40-50 hour weeks
✔ Monday to Friday work with only occasional Saturdays
✔ Mix of local Wellington and North Island travel
✔ Variety of trucks, loads, and work assignments
✔ Opportunity to gain or further develop Hiab experience
✔ Meal allowances and accommodation covered when away
✔ Ongoing training and development
✔ Long-term job security with a respected NZ business

 The Role

Based in Lower Hutt, you'll operate a range of Class 4 and Class 5 vehicles across Wellington and the wider North Island.

One of the biggest attractions of this role is the variety. Rather than being stuck doing the same run every day, you'll be driving different trucks, handling a range of loads, and gaining exposure to Hiab work, keeping the role interesting and helping you broaden your skills.

The role includes:

  • Local and North Island deliveries
  • 0-3 overnight trips per week
  • Load securing, chaining and tarping
  • Hiab operations (training available)
  • Working safely and professionally at all times

 What You'll Bring

  • Class 5 licence
  • Minimum 2 years' Class 5 driving experience
  • Experience with load restraint, chaining and tarping
  • Clean driving and criminal record
  • Strong focus on health and safety
  • Physically fit and happy to get involved when required
  • NZ based and full working rights

Hiab experience is an advantage but not essential. 

 If you're looking for a long-term role with stable hours, quality equipment, and plenty of variety to keep things interesting, we'd love to hear from you.

Natalie Lotter | 04 568 0375 /natalie.lotter@enterprise.co.nz

job.title: Carpenter/Experienced Landscaper
job.description:
Carpenter / Experienced Landscaper – Construction Team

We are looking for a skilled Carpenter or Experienced Landscaper to join our client’s Construction Team. This is a hands-on role building outdoor infrastructure and landscape construction projects for a company committed to providing sustainable solutions across landscapes, water, and environmental projects throughout New Zealand.

If you enjoy working outdoors, take pride in your craftsmanship, and have experience building structures, formwork, decking, or landscape construction, we'd love to hear from you.

About the Role

This is a long term, temporary role with a high chance of permanent employment. However, if you are between jobs, have plans ahead and need a role to tide you over for a few months, this could suit you.

Working alongside the Construction Team, you will be involved in the construction of a wide range of landscape and civil projects, including decking, fencing, retaining structures, concrete formwork, and outdoor amenities.

Key Responsibilities

• Measure, cut, and install timber formwork/boxing for concrete paths, driveways, garden edging, and structural foundations
• Construct fences, gates, screens, pergolas & retaining walls
• Prepare and assemble formwork ready for concrete pours
• Construct sub-frames and install decking, custom seating, stairs, and balustrades
• Assist with pouring, screeding, and finishing concrete
• Safely operate a range of hand and power tools
• Follow all company health and safety policies and procedures
• Work collaboratively with team members to deliver projects to a high standard

What We're Looking For

• Proven experience with timber construction and outdoor structures

• Strong work ethic and commitment to quality workmanship
• Good physical fitness and ability to work outdoors in varying conditions
• A proactive attitude and willingness to work as part of a team
• Strong focus on health and safety

job.title: Electrical Dairy Technician
job.description:
Electrical Dairy Technician

We are looking for a qualified Electrician who enjoys varied, hands-on technical work in the dairy industry. This is a field-based role providing specialist electrical and maintenance support to dairy farms across the Rangiora and North Canterbury region.


If you like solving problems on-site, working with both electrical and mechanical systems, and delivering great service to farmers, this is an excellent opportunity.

About the role

  • Install, service, and repair milking machines and dairy equipment
  • Carry out electrical fault-finding, repairs, and installations on farms
  • Perform servicing, testing, and compliance checks on dairy systems
  • Undertake mechanical repairs, including pumps, motors, and basic fabrication/welding
  • Provide on-farm troubleshooting and technical support to customers
  • Mentor and support a junior Electrical Technician working towards registration

About You

  • Full EWRB Electrical Licence (practising licence)
  • Strong practical electrical and fault-finding skills
  • Hands-on mechanical aptitude (pumps, motors, dairy equipment)
  • Reliable, customer-focused, with a positive attitude
  • Full NZ work rights and ability to work locally in Rangiora/North Canterbury
  • Previous experience with dairy milking equipment or farm machinery
  • Welding and fabrication skills

What’s on Offer

  • Permanent full-time role based in Rangiora
  • Competitive hourly rate of $40 – $45 per hour (depending on experience)
  • Regular hours (7.30am – 4pm) with some flexibility during peak season
  • On-call roster (approximately every 10–12 weeks)
  • Ongoing training and development opportunities
  • Supportive team environment with real job variety
  • This is a rare chance to use your electrical qualification in a specialised, rewarding field role with strong job security in the dairy industry.

Apply Now

Please send your CV and a short cover note outlining your electrical experience and why you’re interested in this role. Applications will be processed as they are received.

job.title: Mig Welding
job.description:
Step into a hands-on welding role where your precision and technical expertise directly support high-quality fabrication work for a busy Wellington workshop.

This fixed-term opportunity is ideal for a skilled MIG welder who thrives in a safety-focused environment and takes pride in producing clean, reliable welds to specification.

About the Role:
You will carry out MIG welding and associated fabrication tasks to deliver components and structures that meet strict quality and safety standards.
Working from blueprints and technical drawings, you will ensure accurate interpretation and execution, contributing to efficient project delivery and minimal rework.

Key Responsibilities:
* Perform MIG welding on a variety of metals in accordance with job specifications and workshop procedures.
* Interpret blueprints and technical drawings to determine welding sequences, dimensions, and fabrication requirements.
* Carry out metal preparation, cutting, and fitting to ensure correct alignment and joint configuration before welding.
* Use welding and workshop tools, including grinders, clamps, and measuring equipment, to support fabrication and finishing.
* Inspect welds for defects, identify root causes, and carry out repairs to restore structural integrity and appearance.
* Conduct weld quality checks and basic non-destructive testing as required to verify compliance with standards.
* Maintain a clean, organised work area and handle equipment in line with workshop safety protocols.
* Collaborate with supervisors and team members to meet production targets and adjust work plans as jobs progress.

Key Requirements:
* Proven experience in MIG welding in a fabrication or workshop environment.
* Strong ability to read and interpret blueprints, technical drawings, and welding symbols.
* Practical experience in metal fabrication, cutting, and fitting for welded assemblies.
* Solid understanding of welding safety standards and safe workshop practices.
* Competence in identifying common weld defects and carrying out effective repair techniques.
* Familiarity with basic weld inspection methods and quality control procedures.
* Reliable, detail-focused approach with the ability to work to set timeframes on a fixed-term basis.

Desirable Skills:
* Exposure to working with different materials and metallurgical properties in welding applications.
* Experience with basic non-destructive testing methods for weld quality assessment.
* Ability to suggest improvements in fabrication processes to reduce defects and rework.
* Previous experience in a similar role within a production or engineering workshop in New Zealand.

Qualifications:
* Trade qualification or certificate in welding, fabrication, or a related discipline is preferred.
* Recognised MIG welding tickets or certifications are advantageous.
* Relevant health and safety training (e.g. workshop safety, hazard management) is beneficial.

If you are a skilled MIG welder looking to contribute to quality fabrication work on a fixed-term basis in Wellington, we’d like to hear from you.

job.title: Service Manager

Location: Dunedin | Employment Type: Permanent, Full-Time | Salary: Up to $140,000 + company vehicle

Are you a commercially minded leader who knows the plumbing and service industry inside out? Our client, a New Zealand-owned building services company delivering plumbing, drainage, gasfitting, electrical, mechanical and HVAC services nationwide, is looking for a Service Manager to lead their Dunedin plumbing service division.

This is a key leadership role for someone who can build a strong team, deliver commercially and take a successful business unit to the next level.

About the Role
Reporting to the Regional Manager, you'll run the day-to-day operations of the Dunedin service business unit. You'll lead the service trades and office staff, and be accountable for profit targets and business development.

Key Responsibilities
  • Own P&L performance, spotting opportunities and areas for improvement
  • Grow domestic and structured service work, including pull-through work
  • Support service contracts across the South Island
  • Oversee quoting and pricing, following up to win work and protect margin
  • Manage key accounts and make sure customer expectations are met
  • Work with the service coordination team to maximise trades utilisation
  • Collaborate with the Dunedin contracting teams to support the wider branch
  • Lead hiring, development, performance and remuneration reviews (HR support available)
  • Champion health and safety, including audits and critical risk management
What You'll Bring
Essential
  • Proven experience in senior management, operational leadership or service management
  • Strong commercial acumen, including P&L and budget management
  • A track record in business development and revenue growth
  • Proven people leadership and the ability to build a high-performing team
  • Strong understanding of the plumbing and service industry
  • Excellent communication, organisation and decision-making skills
  • Full, clean New Zealand Driver Licence
Desirable

Why Apply?
The package is up to $140,000 plus a company vehicle, in a permanent leadership role with an established NZ-owned operator that invests in its people. You'll have real scope to shape and grow the division.

If you're an experienced service or operations leader from the plumbing or trade services industry, APPLY NOW.

job.title: Manufacturing Technician / Process Technician
job.description:
Manufacturing Technician / Process Technician
We're partnering with a well-established New Zealand manufacturer to recruit a Manufacturing Technician for their Ashburton operation.
 
This is a hands-on technical role where you'll play a key part in ensuring highly automated production equipment is operating efficiently, producing quality products, and meeting customer demand. You'll be involved in machine setup, product changeovers, troubleshooting, process optimisation, and continuous improvement initiatives.
 
Working alongside an experienced team, you'll have the opportunity to develop specialist skills within a unique manufacturing environment. Whether your background is in plastics, food manufacturing, dairy processing, packaging, engineering, or industrial production, we're keen to hear from people with strong mechanical aptitude and a desire to learn.
 
About the Role
Working as part of a close-knit production team, you'll support the setup, operation, and optimisation of specialised manufacturing equipment while ensuring quality and production targets are achieved.
 
This role will involve:
  • Assisting with machine setups and product changeovers
  • Changing moulds and tooling on production equipment
  • Monitoring machine performance and product quality
  • Troubleshooting process and equipment issues
  • Making machine and process adjustments to improve efficiency
  • Supporting production uptime and minimising downtime
  • Assisting with new technology and automation projects
About you
You'll enjoy working with machinery, solving problems, and finding ways to improve processes. While plastics manufacturing experience would be advantageous, we're also keen to hear from candidates who have worked in other manufacturing or processing environments.
 
You’ll bring:
  • Experience working within a manufacturing or production environment
  • Strong mechanical aptitude and problem-solving ability
  • Good attention to detail and commitment to quality
  • Ability to manage changing priorities and work as part of a team
  • A willingness to learn specialised manufacturing processes
Most importantly, you’ll be:
  • Hands-on and mechanically minded
  • Proactive and eager to learn
  • Reliable and committed
  • Process-driven with a strong attention to detail
  • Comfortable taking ownership and responsibility
  • A team player with a practical, can-do attitude 
What’s on offer
  • Monday - Friday, day shift (7.30am – 4.30pm) 
  • Competitive hourly rate and overtime opportunities
  • Ongoing training and development
  • Exposure to advanced manufacturing technology, robotics and automation
  • Supportive team and strong culture
  • Long-term career opportunity with a growing business
This is a fantastic opportunity to join a business that is investing in technology, automation, and its people. If you're mechanically minded, enjoy understanding how machinery works, and want to build a long-term career in manufacturing, we'd love to hear from you.
 
‘Apply now’ applications will be processed as they are received.
